content_units: Austin Lease Exit Snapshot
This tenant is leaving about   5.5 months early   on a 12-month lease. Based on the lease terms provided, the main financial paths are usually:
-   Replacement tenant approved by landlord  : exposure may be limited, depending on the lease and any gap before the new tenant starts.
-   Early termination fee  :   2 months’ rent = $3,700
-   Security deposit at stake  :   $1,000  , usually still subject to lawful deductions for damages/unpaid amounts.
Working context
- Lease start:   2025-08-01
- Planned move-out:   2026-02-15
- Monthly rent:   $1,850
- Early termination fee:   $3,700
- Security deposit:   $1,000
- This is   general information only, not legal advice  .
Move-Out Review and Cost Checklist
Item   What to review or do   Why it matters   Estimated amount
Lease clause   Read early termination, re-letting, notice, and move-out sections   Confirms whether fee replaces future rent or is added to it   $0 to $3,700+
Notice requirement   Check how much written notice is required and where it must be sent   Late/defective notice can increase rent owed   Varies
Replacement tenant option   Confirm process, screening standard, timing, and who markets the unit   May reduce total exposure if approved quickly   $0 to several weeks of rent
Early termination fee   Verify whether   2 months’ rent   is the full charge or only one part of the charge   Some leases try to combine fee + rent until re-rented     $3,700
February prorated rent   Estimate rent owed through   2026-02-15   if not already paid   Mid-month move-out often creates a prorated amount   About   $925
Rent after move-out gap   Ask whether rent continues until replacement tenant starts   Biggest variable if no replacement is found quickly   Up to about   $10,175   for remaining term
Security deposit   Confirm whether it can be applied to unpaid rent/fees and what deductions may be taken   Deposit may offset some balance but may also be withheld for damage     $1,000
Condition charges   Review cleaning, repairs, carpet, keys, repainting, utilities   Move-out charges can add to exposure   Varies
Practical review points
- Check whether the lease says the   2-month fee is the exclusive remedy   or whether the landlord may also charge:
- rent until re-rented,
- advertising/re-letting costs,
- concessions given to a new tenant,
- cleaning/repair charges.
- Check whether the lease requires:
-   written notice   by a specific method,
- a minimum notice period,
- payment of the fee   before   release is effective,
- surrender of keys/possession by a certain date.
- Review any clause about   subletting vs. replacement tenants  . Those are often treated differently.
Questions to Put in Writing to the Landlord
Option 1:   Termination terms confirmation     Ask for a written breakdown of all charges that would apply if you vacate on 2026-02-15   Key attribute: confirms whether $3,700 is the full exit cost
Request terms

Option 2:   Replacement tenant process     Ask what qualification standards apply, how quickly applications are reviewed, and whether you may help find candidates   Key attribute: may reduce rent exposure
Review tenant info
Option 3:   Rent obligation after surrender     Ask whether rent continues until a new tenant starts and whether the landlord will actively market the unit   Key attribute: biggest cost variable
Learn basics

Option 4:   Deposit handling and move-out inspection     Ask for a pre-move-out inspection, cleaning expectations, and where the itemized deposit notice will be sent   Key attribute: helps reduce deduction disputes
Deposit rules
Best questions to ask
- If I move out on   2026-02-15  , what exact amounts will I owe under the lease?
- Is the   2 months’ rent fee   the entire early termination charge, or can additional rent/fees also be charged?
- If I provide a qualified replacement tenant, what approval criteria will you use?
- How long does approval usually take after an application is submitted?
- Will you market the unit, and when will marketing begin?
- If a new tenant starts before the original lease end date, how will my balance be recalculated?
- Can my   $1,000 security deposit   be applied to any unpaid rent or termination charges?
- Can we do a   pre-move-out walkthrough   so I can cure issues before surrender?
- What cleaning, patching, key return, and utility shutoff steps do you require?
- Where should I send notice, keys, and my forwarding address?
Financial Exposure Estimate
Quick math
-   Monthly rent  : $1,850
-   Daily equivalent for rough proration  : about   $60.82   ($1,850 × 12 ÷ 365)
-   Prorated rent through 2026-02-15  : about   $925
-   Early termination fee  :   $3,700
-   Remaining full-term rent after 2026-02-15 to 2026-07-31  : about   $10,175   total face-value remaining rent
Likely scenarios
-   Best case  : approved replacement tenant starts immediately, minimal gap, deposit mostly returned.
- Possible exposure:   small turnover costs + any short rent gap
-   Fee-based exit case  : landlord accepts lease termination on payment of   $3,700  , plus any unpaid prorated February rent and lawful damages.
- Rough exposure before deposit treatment: about   $4,625   if February 1-15 rent is still owed
-   Higher-risk case  : no replacement tenant is found quickly and lease allows fee plus continuing rent until re-rented.
- Exposure could rise well above   $3,700  , potentially approaching some or all of the   $10,175   remaining rent, reduced by any rent received from a replacement tenant
Simple estimate formula
Formula:   Estimated exposure = unpaid prorated rent + termination fee or post-move-out rent gap + re-letting/repair charges − deposit returned
Deposit impact
- If the landlord lawfully keeps the full   $1,000 deposit  , your out-of-pocket amount increases by that amount.
- If the deposit is returned in full, it reduces your net cost pressure.
- Do   not   assume the deposit automatically covers the last month’s rent unless the landlord agrees in writing or the lease allows it.
Records to Keep Before and After Move-Out
- Signed lease and any addenda
- All emails/texts with the landlord or property manager
- Your written move-out notice and proof it was delivered
- Written responses about termination charges or replacement tenant rules
- Photos/video of the unit at move-out, dated if possible
- Move-in condition form and old move-in photos
- Receipts for cleaning, repairs, carpet service, and key return
- Utility final bills and shutoff/transfer confirmations
- Replacement tenant leads you forwarded and any application timestamps
- Ledger showing rent paid, fee paid, deposit claimed, and any balance demanded
- Forwarding address notice
- Copy of any final account statement or deposit itemization
